observedFailureFamily: The model conflated S- and R-warfarin clearance, misattributed a principal pathway, and treated the enzyme effect of a co-medication as though it were necessarily the drug's own clearance route.
guard: Require enantiomer-specific pathway attribution; no interaction-specific dose adjustment may be inferred from pathway mapping alone.

observedFailureFamily: The model described IC50 as binding affinity and treated it as interchangeable with Kd or Ki without checking assay conditions or inhibition mechanism.
guard: Keep assay potency, inhibition constant, and equilibrium dissociation constant distinct; use Cheng–Prusoff only under the competitive-inhibition assumptions.

observedFailureFamily: The model inferred functional hyperaldosteronism from adrenal morphology, confused human and feline values, or transferred an assay interval as a disease cutoff.
guard: Require feline species context and assay identity; a healthy-cat LC–MS/MS reference interval is not a validated PHA cutoff, and imaging alone is insufficient.

observedFailureFamily: The model overgeneralized the best-known canine MDR1/ABCB1 phenotype and assumed cats cannot have documented ABCB1-associated ivermectin sensitivity.
guard: Distinguish a feline case report from prevalence estimates, breed-wide conclusions, or universal screening/dose recommendations.

observedFailureFamily: The model confused the FHL/FDL tendon crossing with the nearby medial plantar nerve and described the named knot as a nerve structure.
guard: Name the structure first, then state the adjacent nerve's separate origin and course.

observedFailureFamily: The model omitted the factor of two in calculated urine osmolality, interpreted the urine osmolal gap as a direct ammonium assay, or overinterpreted UAG in hippurate excretion.
reason: The primary full-text sources inspected for this specific discussion do not have a redistribution license accepted by the app's specialized-KB builder. Keep the error in the internal regression audit; do not embed source text or expose an unsupported clinical rule to students.

observedFailureFamily: The model supplied unprovided histology or patient findings while explaining a plausible FH/fumarate pathway.
reason: This is not a missing fact to add to the specialist library. Existing lesson prompt requirements already tell the model to verify every stated datum against the original question and never invent missing case data.

observedFailureFamily: The model invented pH, bicarbonate, renin, aldosterone, appetite, and chloride data, and transferred human interpretation thresholds to a cat.
guard: Keep original-case facts separate from retrieved expert context; do not populate absent patient measurements or infer primary versus secondary disease without supporting evidence.

observedFailureFamily: The model calculated each amide local anaesthetic against its own maximum independently and ignored additive CNS/cardiovascular toxicity across combined agents.
guard: Use the cited fractional-dose heuristic for combined-agent procedures, preserve its pharmacokinetic limitations, and independently account for vasoconstrictor exposure.

observedFailureFamily: The model assumed LAST must begin with a classic CNS prodrome and failed to account for delayed or cardiovascular-first presentation, or for sedation masking early neurologic symptoms.
guard: Do not rule out LAST solely because the classic CNS prodrome is absent; match the setting and use source-specific observation and monitoring guidance.

observedFailureFamily: The model used FH loss/fumarate biology to label a tumour hereditary HLRCC without germline evidence, or treated fumarate accumulation as uniquely diagnostic of FH loss.
guard: Distinguish FH-deficient tumour biology from proof of inherited HLRCC; require the relevant clinical/genetic evidence and do not treat one metabolite or mechanism as a definitive diagnosis.

observedFailureFamily: The model invented a histologic subtype or claimed morphology alone proves FH-deficient RCC when the case stem did not provide those features or confirmatory work-up.
guard: State only histology actually supplied; distinguish a differential clue from a definitive integrated pathology diagnosis.

observedFailureFamily: The model imported the canine ABCB1 deletion nomenclature or breed-risk narrative into a feline case without species-specific evidence.
guard: Identify the species before naming the variant; do not transfer canine nucleotide deletion notation or prevalence assumptions to cats.

observedFailureFamily: The model treated an in-vitro transporter inhibitor IC50 as an animal plasma toxicity threshold, a dose, or a clinical interaction magnitude.
guard: Keep cell-assay inhibition concentrations separate from whole-animal exposure, clinical toxicity and dose recommendations unless an in-vivo study directly validates the bridge.

observedFailureFamily: The model converted a commonly cited interaction percentage into a universal warfarin dose reduction without patient-specific INR, current dose, time course, genotype or interacting medicines.
guard: Do not issue a universal dose-change percentage from interaction name or pathway alone; use current anticoagulation guidance and patient-specific INR/clinical monitoring.

observedFailureFamily: The model used a genotype result as a stand-alone warfarin prescription and ignored clinical covariates or confused initial-dose algorithms with maintenance dosing.
guard: Use the exact validated algorithm and full required inputs; distinguish initial dose prediction from stable maintenance therapy.
